name: Spot Temporal Disturbances
summary: Keep an exact sense of the current time and notice the ripples left behind by Time magick: rewinds, loops, triggers, anchor points and travellers popping out of the timestream.
system: Noticing a disturbance is usually a Perception + Awareness roll; bigger Effects leave bigger ripples. They can show up as waves in the air, ghostly sounds from other times, ticking clocks, slow-motion patches or deja vu.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: The Basics
Time Distortion and Travel: Temporal Disturbances

name: Speed Yourself Up or Slow Others Down
summary: Stretch time around yourself to get extra actions in a turn, or squeeze it around someone else to take actions away from them.
system: Two successes per extra action gained, or per action taken away from another character. Speeding yourself up does not count toward the Repeated Time Effects penalty.
coincidentalIf: you take only one or two extra actions a turn, which can pass as a burst of speed; three or more a turn is vulgar

name: The Perfect Moment
summary: Sense exactly when to act so a mundane task goes better: the right moment to walk in, crack a joke, throw a punch or juggle. Harder, more involved tasks call on extra Spheres to read the situation.
system: Cast the Effect with your focus first. Each Arete success then lowers the difficulty of one Attribute + Ability roll by 1, to at most -3. It cannot lower an Arete roll, except when used to prepare a ritual in advance, and even then by no more than -3. Needs time to set up, so it is little use in a fast fight.

name: Total Recall
summary: Relive a past event from someone's own memory in full sensory detail, as if it were happening now. The memory stays as subjective as the original experience, though the viewer may catch details missed at the time.
system: More successes give a clearer and more accurate memory. Nothing the person could not perceive back then can be recovered. Whether it can recall things that have not happened yet is up to the Storyteller.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Total Recall

name: Thicken the Walls of Time
summary: Make the local flow of time heavy and stubborn so that other mages have a harder time working Time magick near you.
system: Each success you score takes one success off another mage's Time Effects. Past five successes, time around you starts to stutter: clocks skip, speech and movement drag, and everyone feels heavy. That is easy to miss out in the wilds but obvious in busy places like cities or parties.
coincidentalIf: you use no more than five successes

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Thickening the Walls of Time

name: Time Loop
summary: Freeze an area and roll it back to an earlier moment while you alone keep moving, so you can act differently the second time around.
system: Counts as a Magickal Feat of Time: 3 successes for yourself, 4 for one other person, 5 for a few people or a 10-foot square, 8 for a 25-foot square, 10-20 for larger areas, 20+ for a huge area. Add 2 successes per turn rewound. Going back adds +3 difficulty and multiplies Paradox by the turns rewound. Each further Time Effect in the same scene must score more successes than the one before.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Rewinding Time
Time Distortion and Travel: Magickal Feats of Time
Common Magickal Effects: Time and Distance

name: Reboot Another Person
summary: Send someone else back a few turns with their memories intact, so they can replay events knowing what is coming. The rest of the world repeats itself until they change something.
system: Each rebooted person beyond yourself costs 3 or more extra successes on top of the 2 per turn rewound. Rewinding adds +3 difficulty and stacks Paradox per turn. The Storyteller may cap reboots at five turns. Cannot undo a vampire's curse. Rebooting only yourself takes Life 3, Mind 1 and Time 3.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Rewinding Time

name: Accelerated Aging or Youth
summary: Fast-forward the aging of a person, creature or object until it withers or crumbles, or run it backward to make it young or new again. It works on the whole subject at once, never on a single part.
system: Successes depend on how much aging, not how many years: 3 minor, 4 noticeable, 5 severe, 8 decrepit, 10-20 near destruction, 20+ aged out of existence. Reversing age adds +3 difficulty. Vampires, werecreatures, mummies and fae just take lethal damage equal to the successes and recover their years; spirits and ghosts are immune.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Accelerated Youth or Decay
Time Distortion and Travel: Aging the Night-Folk

name: Disrupt Heartbeat Rhythm
summary: Throw a person's heartbeat out of its natural rhythm. You can upset the timing of the heart, but you cannot run it in a different time-stream from the rest of the body.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Accelerated Youth or Decay

name: Temporal Anchor Point
summary: Fix a point in time you can return to after travelling or stepping out of time. The anchor can be a set alarm or clock, a mantra, an icon, a place or a memorable staged event, depending on your focus.
system: Without an anchor, any trip through time is one-way and the Storyteller decides where you end up. Returning also needs Time 4 and only works if the anchor still exists and you can reach it. Anyone with Time 1 can spot an anchor, so hide it well. Setting it in a Sanctum or other secluded place makes the return less likely to draw Paradox.

optional.purpose: return to the anchor from far away in space

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Freeze a Moment in Time
summary: Stop a single event in mid-motion, like a falling glass, a bullet or a car crash. When the freeze ends, everything carries on along its old path unless you changed it in the meantime.
system: Base successes by size of event: a falling teacup 1, a looming train wreck 5-10 or more. Add successes for longer durations by the dividing successes chart (one day +2, six months +5). Anyone else touching the frozen scene ends it at once; you can end it whenever you like.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Temporal Suspension
summary: Put one subject into stasis: stop a body's life processes, hold an object, energy or place unchanged, keep something from decaying, lock a spirit outside time, or even hold a feeling, memory or train of thought in place.
system: Lasts the normal Duration; extend it with the dividing successes rule. Small subjects are easy (a mouse, 1-2 successes); big or complex ones like a tank or a set of memories take 5 or more.

combos.note: stop decay; also add the Sphere of the place, object or body
a memory, idea or state of sanity

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Contingency Trigger Effect
summary: Hang another Effect in time so it only goes off when a chosen condition is met: a kiss, a cat crossing a doorstep, a band finally splitting up.
system: Base successes depend on the scale of the held Effect, per the Feats of Time Magick chart; it lasts until the condition happens. While waiting it sits in a temporal ripple that Time mages can notice and counter.

optional.purpose: tie the held Effect to an object
tie the held Effect to a living being

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Time Bubble Prison
summary: Wrap a creature, energy, object or spirit in a bubble outside both time and space, cut off from the world until it ends.
system: A Godlike feat: 20 or more successes, plus 2 per step on the Time-Sphere Timelines chart, and each step adds two layers of Paradox. Fifty years takes at least 24 successes and eight times the normal Paradox.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Sidestep Time
summary: Step sideways out of the timestream so nothing outside can touch you. You can still hit or handle things, but they only feel it once the Effect ends, so a victim gets punched by someone they never saw.
system: Turn by turn only. You cannot cast magick while sidestepped, and anything already inside you (poison, sickness, wounds) keeps working. Bringing someone along costs 2 more successes and 1 more Paradox per person.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Time Travel
summary: Leave the present and travel forward or back through time, stepping out again in the same place at another time. Long trips can change you so much that you no longer fit into the life you left.
system: Out of combat only. Successes: 2 for each step on the Timelines chart (within a year 1, five years 2, 20 years 3, 50 years 4, 100 years 5, 500 years 6, 1000+ years 10); 50 years back takes 8. Going back adds +3 difficulty, is always vulgar and adds two layers of Paradox per step (50 years back: eight times the usual Paradox). Without an anchor point the trip is one-way. Sending another person a few turns costs 4 successes plus 2 per turn.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity
